# pcd_compute_host_drain (Action)

Moves every instance off a hypervisor that is in maintenance, as the PCD UI's Enable Maintenance Mode does after it disables the host: active and paused instances live-migrate, shut-off and suspended ones cold-migrate (and are confirmed), and the scheduler picks each target. Instances are moved one at a time and each move is checked: an instance that is still on the host afterward is reported with Nova's reason, and the others still move. Instances in any other state (resizing, rescued, in error, shelved, or with a task in progress) are left in place with a warning. When the host was put in maintenance the PCD UI's way (`pcd_compute_service` with `status = "maintenance"`), every instance moved is tagged with the maintenance ID first, so the UI's maintenance progress view tracks it. Running the action again moves whatever is still on the host. The host must already be disabled, so nothing new lands on it meanwhile; on a host that still takes new instances the action moves nothing and warns. Instances may move to another cluster: one managed by Terraform with `availability_zone` set then plans a replacement, so check the plan after a drain. Requires an admin token and Terraform 1.14 or later.

~> **Requires Terraform 1.14 or later.** Actions are a Terraform 1.14 feature. Resources and data sources are
expected to keep working on older versions, but a configuration that declares an `action` block or an
`action_trigger` does not load.

An action runs only when it is invoked and stores nothing in state. Invoke it from a resource's
`lifecycle` `action_trigger` (on `after_create` or `after_update`), or once from the command line:

```shell
terraform apply -invoke=action.pcd_compute_host_drain.<name>
```

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.14"
}

data "pcd_host" "hyp1" {
  name = "hyp1.example.com"
}

# The host in maintenance, as the PCD UI's Enable Maintenance Mode leaves it.
resource "pcd_compute_service" "hyp1" {
  host_id = data.pcd_host.hyp1.id
  status  = "maintenance"
}

# Moves every instance off the host; run it once the host is in maintenance:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.pcd_compute_host_drain.hyp1
# Running it again moves whatever is still there.
action "pcd_compute_host_drain" "hyp1" {
  config {
    host_id = pcd_compute_service.hyp1.host_id
  }
}

# Or drain on every entry into maintenance: each one writes a new
# disabled_reason, which changes this resource's input and triggers the action.
# Leaving maintenance changes it too, so the condition keeps a move to
# "enabled" or "disabled" from triggering a drain ("disabled" clears the reason
# but still takes the host out of scheduling, which the action would drain).
resource "terraform_data" "drain_hyp1" {
  input = pcd_compute_service.hyp1.disabled_reason

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events    = [after_create, after_update]
      condition = pcd_compute_service.hyp1.status == "maintenance"
      actions   = [action.pcd_compute_host_drain.hyp1]
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host_id` (String) The hypervisor's resmgr host UUID, as `pcd_compute_service.<name>.host_id` or `data.pcd_host.<name>.id`.

### Optional

- `region` (String) The region the hypervisor is in. Defaults to the provider's region.
- `skip_powered_off` (Boolean) Leave shut-off instances on the host, as the UI's "skip powered-off VMs" does. Suspended instances still move. Defaults to `false`.
